objective.statement: Use a dot to make a note half as long again.
successCriteria: I know a dot after a note adds half of the note's own length.
I know a dotted crotchet lasts 1½ beats, a dotted minim 3 and a dotted semibreve 6.
I can tell a dot from a tie.

explanation.text: A dot written after a note makes it longer: it adds half of the note's own value.

music.textAlternative: A dotted minim, a dotted crotchet and a dotted quaver, labelled with their lengths: 3, one and a half, and three quarters.

explanation.caption: Dotted minim: 3 beats. Dotted crotchet: 1½ beats. Dotted quaver: ¾ beat.

explanation.text: A minim is 2 beats, and half of 2 is 1, so a dotted minim is 3 beats. A crotchet is 1 beat and half of 1 is ½, so a dotted crotchet is 1½ beats.
A dot does the same job as a tie to a note half the size. A dotted minim sounds exactly like a minim tied to a crotchet.
To find a dotted note's length: take the note's beats, then add half of that.

music.textAlternative: Two four-beat bars. The first has a dotted minim and a crotchet. The second has a dotted crotchet, a quaver and a minim.

steps: Press Play all. In bar one, hold the dotted minim for three beats, then the crotchet takes the fourth.
In bar two, the dotted crotchet lasts a beat and a half and the quaver fills the other half.
Both bars make four beats: dotted notes fit neatly with their short partners.
demonstration.textAlternative: Two bars of four beats built with dotted notes and a short note to complete each beat.

feedback.correct: The dotted note matches the tied pair.

mistakes.halved-or-doubled: That value is twice (or half) as long. Count it in crotchet beats and compare.
mistakes.dot-misread: Remember: a dot adds half of the note's own value. Work out that half, then add it.
mistakes.note-rest-confusion: Check the shape carefully. A rest that hangs below its line lasts longer than one that sits on top of it.
mistakes.tie-dot-confusion: A tie joins two notes into one sound, so add both values together.
mistakes.tuplet-ignored: Those notes are a tuplet, so they share a different amount of time. Look at the number written over them.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Try counting each value in crotchet beats.
